images.title: Fourths and thirds in twelfths
images.purpose: Show that 3/4 and 2/3 can be taken from each other only after both are cut into the same unit, twelfths: 9/12 − 8/12 = 1/12.
images.composition: Two strips of exactly the same length stacked one above the other with a wide gap, left edges lined up, and one equation centred below.
images.exact_structure: Top strip, one whole glass: cut by solid lines into 4 equal parts, and each part split by thin grey #6B7280 dashed lines into 3, making 12 equal small parts; the 9 leftmost small parts are filled, the first 8 teal #0072B2 and the 9th reddish purple #CC79A7. Bottom strip, the same length: cut by solid lines into 3 equal parts, and each part split by grey dashed lines into 4, making 12 equal small parts; the 8 leftmost are filled amber #E69F00. All small-part edges line up vertically. Exactly 2 strips, 24 small parts.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
strips of different lengths, or twelfths that do not line up between the two strips
images.takeaway: Cut both into one common unit, then take away.
images.description: Two strips of the same length: 3/4 re-cut into 12 equal parts shows 9 filled, and 2/3 re-cut into 12 equal parts shows 8 filled; the one extra part on the top strip is 1/12.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the one purple part that has no amber part under it and name its size.

image_decisions.why: Re-cutting fourths and thirds into the same twelfths is a picture idea; two aligned strips carry it cleanly.
